A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PQM research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support matching retained content despite reformatting and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original MATH500 and GSM-Plus verification experiments, backbone and loss ablations, empirical validation, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds beam-search, training-data-size, and ranking-behavior experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Appendix C adds using PQM to guide beam search during generation, extending its inference use beyond completed-trajectory verification. The reward-model architecture, Q-value formulation, and comparative training losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Math-Shepherd training data, MATH500 and GSM-Plus evaluation, and Math-Step-DPO-10K validation trajectories. Added search procedures, policy configurations, and training subsets retain the same mathematical-reasoning coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains ORM, BCE, MSE with binary labels, and MSE with MCTS labels. The added appendix experiments reuse BCE, existing loss variants, and baseline policy sampling; no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: Appendix C substantially extends evaluation design with beam search using beam size 8 and temperature 0.7, additional Llama-8B and Eurus policy configurations, and training on random 25%, 50%, and 75% subsets with margin 4. It also introduces ranking-agreement evaluation, including 2,048 sampled training cases. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test sensitivity to training-data quantity, loss formulation and margin during beam search, and whether BCE and PQM produce different rankings within and across solutions. These substantially broaden the supporting analyses beyond v1's retained loss ablations, theoretical validation, ceiling comparison, and case studies.

E5.justification: The existing variability displays in Figures 3–4 are retained. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests; the new ranking-agreement percentages are descriptive results.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–6 and retained case-study values are unchanged. New Tables 7–9 report beam-search performance, search ablations, and training-size results; for example, Eurus-7b-sft scores 29.2 with PQM versus 24.2 with BCE in Table 7. New ranking results include 29.18% identical within-solution rankings, 0% identical candidate-solution rankings, and differing rankings on 62.79% of sampled training cases.

T1.justification: The Q-value definition, Assumption 3.1, supporting lemmas and proofs, Theorem 3.5, and Appendix D corollaries are unchanged. Section 3.3 adds a roadmap explaining the existing derivation, without revising its mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same ranking-based PRM contribution, classification-as-a-special-case claim, and headline MATH500 comparison of 39.8% versus 51.4%. The added experiments do not redefine the main contribution statements.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly attributes larger self-consistency gains to policy-model capacity. Appendix C adds interpretations concerning search guidance, sample efficiency, and differences between BCE and PQM rankings. Appendix F's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C supplies settings for the new search, subset-training, and ranking experiments. Existing hardware, software, batching details, and the code link remain unchanged. Reproducibility is limited by the new beam-search prose naming Llama-3-8B-Instruct while Table 7 names Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Im and Li (2024), Khanov et al. (2024), and Yuan et al. (2024), covering alignment research and the additional policy model. The substantive positioning against classification-based PRMs, MCTS methods, and step-level preference optimization remains stable.

P1.justification: The section sequence and most prose are retained. Changes include the Section 3.3 explanatory roadmap, additional interpretive paragraphs, localized language corrections, conference-header text, and conversion to author-year citations.

P2.justification: The ICLR format changes typography, text width, headings, headers, and content placement throughout. v2 adds Tables 7–9 and highlights leading entries in Table 3. Existing figures remain, and v1's case-study Tables 7–8 are retained as Tables 10–11.

improvement.justification: Appendix C's guided-search, training-size, and ranking-behavior studies provide useful additional evidence about PQM's applicability and behavior, while Section 3.3 improves explanation. These are incremental gains over the retained core results and theory. The inconsistent Llama identification and absence of uncertainty reporting for the new results limit the strength of the added evidence.
